listen.explanationKey: Why does the flag have 50 stars?
facts: The American flag is red, white and blue.
It has 50 stars, one star for each state.
It has 13 stripes because there were 13 original colonies.

a promise of loyalty to the flag and the United States

help.simpler: This is the flag of the United States.
help.example: You can see it on government buildings and at schools.

story.say: The American flag is red, white and blue.

help.simpler: The flag has three colors: red, white and blue.
help.example: The stripes are red and white. The stars are white on blue.

check.statement: The American flag is red, white and blue.

story.say: It has 50 stars, one star for each state.

help.simpler: Each star stands for one state.
help.example: There are 50 states, so there are 50 stars.
help.why: “One star for each state” is an answer on the test.

help.simpler: The number of stars is the same as the number of states.
help.example: When a new state joined, a new star was added.

story.say: It has 13 stripes because there were 13 original colonies.

help.simpler: Each stripe stands for one of the first 13 colonies.
help.example: Represent means to stand for something.
help.why: “13 original colonies” is an answer on the test.

story.say: The 13 colonies became the first 13 states.

help.simpler: The stripes remember where the country started.
help.example: You learned about the 13 colonies in Unit 4.
help.why: It helps you remember why there are 13 stripes.

listen.explanationKey: The Nation’s first motto was “E Pluribus Unum.” What does that mean?
facts: The nation's first motto was “E Pluribus Unum.” It means “Out of many, one.”
Say it like this: ee PLOOR-ih-bus OO-num.
It says that many people and many states become one country.
The national anthem is “The Star-Spangled Banner.” It is a song about the American flag.

newWords.meaning: a short saying that tells what a group believes

story.say: The nation’s first motto was “E Pluribus Unum.”

help.simpler: A motto is a short saying that tells what a group believes.
help.example: The words are in Latin, an old language.
help.why: The test asks what “E Pluribus Unum” means.

story.say: Say it like this: ee PLOOR-ih-bus OO-num.

help.simpler: Say it slowly, in four parts: ee, PLOOR-ih-bus, OO-num.
help.example: The big letters show which part to say strongly.
help.why: It helps you say the motto out loud.

help.simpler: Many things come together to make one.
help.example: “We all become one” is another answer.
help.why: “Out of many, one” is the answer on the test.

story.say: It says that many people and many states become one country.

help.simpler: People from many places make one country together.
help.why: It explains the meaning of the motto.

story.say: The national anthem is “The Star-Spangled Banner.”
